subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Blind Spot Bias
description: A fast breakdown of Blind Spot Bias for builders.

hook.text: You can spot biases in others instantly. When asked about your own? 'I'm pretty objective.'

buildup.text: Pronin's research found that people see bias as a problem others have. Not themselves. Never.

discovery.text: Blind spot bias: we recognize cognitive biases in others but deny them in our own thinking.

twist.text: Ironically, knowing about biases can make it worse. You think awareness means immunity. It doesn't.

climax.text: The only defense is structured processes that remove human judgment from the equation entirely.

punchline.text: Your biggest bias: thinking you don't have one.

quiz.question: What makes blind spot bias especially dangerous?
options: Knowing about biases can increase false confidence

details.summary: Blind spot bias is the tendency to recognize cognitive biases in others while failing to see them in oneself. People readily identify when others are biased but maintain the illusion that their own judgments are objective and bias-free.
details.whyItMatters: Blind spot bias is uniquely dangerous because it makes all other biases resistant to correction. If you believe you are unbiased, you see no reason to check your reasoning or seek alternative perspectives, leaving all biases unchallenged.
takeaways: People see biases in others more easily than in themselves
Believing you are unbiased makes you more vulnerable to biases
Blind spot bias resists correction because it blocks self-awareness

faq.question: Why can people see biases in others but not in themselves?
faq.answer: People have direct access to their own reasoning, which feels logical and well-founded from the inside. They only see others' conclusions, which look biased from the outside. This asymmetry creates confident but incorrect self-assessment.

faq.question: How can you overcome your own blind spot bias?
faq.answer: Assume you are biased by default and build systems that catch errors. Use checklists, seek diverse perspectives, and treat disagreement as information rather than error. The best protection is accepting that self-assessment of bias is unreliable.
